1.
The instant case arises out of a road accident dated RAKESH RAKESH KUMAR KUMAR SINGH 02.09.2012.

After investigating the matter, the police filed a SINGH Date:
2025.12.03 18:16:29 Detailed Accident Report (DAR) indicating that a road accident +0530 had taken place in which one Pradeep Kumar had suffered certain injuries.
The accident was attributed to the rash/negligent act of a driver of car number DL-6CG-7917.
FIR No.98/2012 was registered and final charge-sheet was also presented before the Ld. Judicial Magistrate against driver Sheesh Pal for offences punishable u/s 279/338 IPC.
2. On receiving of the DAR, the proceedings was initiated.
Driver namely Sheesh Pal and Owner Sindhu Mishra filed their reply.
Insurance company also filed its reply.

On available material, the Ld. Predecessor framed following issues:
1.
Whether petitioner Pradeep Kumar sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident dtd 02.09.2012 due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle no. DL-6CG-7917 by R1?
Whether the petittioner is entitiled to claim compensation, if so, what amount and from whom? ...OPP 3. Relief.
3. During the evidence injured Pradeep Kumar examined himself and was cross examined by the insurance company.
He also examined one Krishan Kumar but this witness was not cross Digitally signed by RAKESH RAKESH KUMAR examined despite opportunity.
Insurance company examined KUMAR SINGH SINGH

Date:
2025.12.03 Amit Kumar and Kuber Dutt Sharma.
The drive absented himself 18:16:35 +0530 during the proceeding and the owner though a period but did so casual conduct.
Arguments have been heard.
The present judgment will dispose of the case.
4. Occurrence of accident is mentioned in the FIR.
Involvement of the offending vehicle is also mentioned so.
Even a charge-sheet was filed against the driver Sheesh Pal.
In such circumstances, it cannot be accepted that the vehicle was not involved.
The insurance company has tried to impeach the credit of injured but it has failed.
The cross-examination of injured Pradeep Kumar does not show any justification as to why he should be doubted on the point of accident, involvement of vehicle and rashness/ negligence.

Insurance company has not summoned the driver as a witness Pardeep Kumar vs Shish Pal on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125768698/
2
neither they have appointed any investigator.
In such circumstances, it is accepted that accident happened due to rash/ negligent driving of offending vehicle.
Issue No. 1 is decided in favour of claimants.
5. We have then to see as to what amount of compensation should be awarded.
6. The injured has not exhibited any medical bill and has further stated that DMRC had reimbursed his medical expenditure.
Therefore, no amount can be allowed on medical treatment.
7. Injured has exhibited his pay slip of Delhi Metro Digitally signed by RAKESH Corporation.

The insurance company has simply suggested that RAKESH KUMAR KUMAR SINGH income proof is false and fabricated document but did not bring SINGH Date:
2025.12.03 18:16:41 +0530 any proof to dispute the same.
However, the injured himself has accepted that he got his salary during the treatment period.
In such circumstances how the injured can claim any loss of income is not clear.

Therefore,
no amount shall be allowed towards loss of income.
There is no disability and therefore there cannot be any loss in earning capacity.
8. Ld.
Counsel for claimant has argued that conveyance charges should be provided to the injured by counting Rs.7,000/- per month for 24 months as the injured had engaged service of a driver.
Injured has examined one Krishan Kumar in support.
Perusal of the testimony shows that this witness is claiming to have been employed as driver from September 2012 to August 2015 at the rate of Rs.7,000/- per month in cash.
This witness however has not provided any detail of vehicle which he was driving.
He has not produced any agreement or terms and conditions for such employment.
He has not explained as to from where to where he was driving the vehicle for the injured.
In such circumstances I am unable to find any justification in the claim of Ld. Counsel.

However,
considering the fact that the injured had suffered grievous injuries requiring hospital visit on multiple occasions, a lump sum amount of Rs.20,000/- on account of conveyance is allowed.
Digitally 9.
The claimant had suffered grievous injury and was even signed by RAKESH RAKESH KUMAR admitted in hospital thrice.

Therefore, on account of pain and KUMAR SINGH SINGH Date:
2025.12.03 18:16:49 suffering Rs.50,000/- is allowed.
As far as special diet is +0530 concerned, a sum of Rs.30,000/- is allowed.
For nursing attendant, a sum of Rs.15,000/- is allowed.
It cannot be denied that a person having suffered grievous injury will have some difficulty in life.
Therefore, in respect of inconvenience caused due to accident, an amount of Rs.20,000/- is also allowed.
The total amount in this manner will be Rs.1,35,000/-.

sentences.text: Respondent Shish Pal (driver) being principal tortfeasor driving offending vehicle in rash/negligent manner is liable to pay compensation along with interest to injured.
The owner Sindhu Mishra will be liable vicariously.

However, since offending vehicle was insured with the insurance company against Third Party Risk so, the insurer being statutorily liable under Section 150 of M.V. Act shall pay the award amount with interest to injured in the absence of any statutory defence under Section 150(2)
of M.V. Act.
11.

However, Ld. Counsel for insurance company wants to avoid the liability on the premise that the insurance company had issued the policy on the basis of earlier insurance policy which was later on found to be fake.
He argues that this should be treated as fundamental breach of conditions and therefore, insurance company should not be made liable for the compensation.
I am however unable to accept this claim of Digitally insurance company.
The company had issued the insurance signed by RAKESH RAKESH KUMAR policy and had taken premium.

The contract stood concluded KUMAR SINGH SINGH Date:
2025.12.03 18:16:59 once both the sides performed their part.
It was for the insurance +0530 company to either refuse or to accept the offer of vehicle owner regarding the insurance.
The company did not refuse and accepted the offer and issued the insurance policy.
In such manner the contract was concluded.
The Ld.
Counsel has not brought any law to my notice which says that it is mandatory for the insurance company to issue new policy on the basis of the earlier one, without verification.
The policy was being issued for a vehicle and that too against third party risk.
Such insurance policy does not even require checking of vehicle.
Had the owner not produced earlier policy, the insurance company still could have issued the new insurance policy at best after verification of vehicle.
It is not the case of insurance company that vehicle was having any defect due to which it would not have issued the policy.
Ld. Counsel for insurance company has argued that owner did not produce the vehicle for inspection.
However, he has not produced any material proof in this respect.
I am of the view that insurance company cannot avoid to compensate a third party when it has already received a premium and issued a policy.

Since the lack of care is on the part of insurance company and further the insurance company has not shown any law regarding issuance of a new policy as a mandate on the basis of earlier policy, I am not inclined to allow the insurance company the right to recover.
12. There is nothing on record to justify withholding interest on the award amount.

Therefore, a simple interest @ 7.5 % per annum is allowed on the Award Amount w.e.f. 01.02.2013 till realization.
13.
Let a separate Award be prepared based on the aforesaid calculation and directions, so that all the concerned persons can comply with the same.
Announced in the open Court RAKESH by RAKESH KUMAR SINGH on 03.12.2025.
